propagation_patterns.pattern: Mixed transit paths through multiple Tier 1 networks

path_inflation_analysis.notes: Minimal path inflation observed, suggesting efficient propagation through existing transit networks

geographic_analysis.transit_network_coverage: Global Tier 1 networks (Telstra, Cogent, Level 3, Tata)

impact_assessment.visibility: 28 out of 39 observed paths (72%) show the hijacked route, indicating significant propagation
impact_assessment.reachability_impact: Traffic destined for 113.20.40.0/22 is being diverted to attacker AS 7029 instead of legitimate owner AS 397373
impact_assessment.duration_impact: Hijack persisted for approximately 12.5 hours from start to end time
impact_assessment.mitigation_difficulty: Moderate - requires coordination with multiple Tier 1 transit networks to filter illegitimate announcements

recommendations: Notify direct upstream providers of AS 7029 to filter hijacked prefix announcements
Coordinate with Tier 1 networks (1299, 6939, 3356, 6453) to implement prefix filters for 113.20.40.0/22 from AS 7029
Legitimate owner AS 397373 should implement RPKI ROA to cryptographically validate prefix ownership
Monitor for similar hijack attempts targeting other prefixes owned by AS 397373
Implement BGP monitoring with real-time alerting for origin AS changes
